A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MEAD and Ab-MDP work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–G are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original reinforcement-learning experiments on 2D Crafting and MiniHack, including transfer, compositional planning, learned abstraction components, and ablations (Section 4 and Appendix F).

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in Section 4 and Appendix F, including MEAD evaluations and baseline comparisons.

M1.justification: Sections 2–3, Algorithm 1, and Appendix C retain the same abstraction, discriminative success model, count-based MCTS exploration, and Dijkstra goal planning. The added factored-MDP discussion does not modify the method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three 2D Crafting environments, five MiniHack skill games, sandbox transfer, and Levitate-then-Freeze compositional task. The robotics examples in Table 1 remain illustrative constructions, not additional evaluations.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain PPO, Dreamer-v3, MuZero, the nonparametric attribute planner, and NCS/k-means comparisons (Figures 4, 17–23). Factored MDPs are newly discussed as related work, without an added evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, budgets, preprocessing, model configurations, and experimental procedures are unchanged. Both retain 200k-frame transfer pretraining, the 100k-transition encoder dataset, and the settings in Appendices D, F, and G.

E4.justification: The model, exploration, embedding, optimization, and learned-component analyses are retained. The single-item failure example and replanning discussion in Appendix B.2.2, and the representation and world-graph analyses in Appendix F, already appear in v2.

E5.justification: Table 6 reports identical seed counts. Both versions retain 95% confidence intervals for main results, standard deviation for encoder accuracy in Figure 6, and standard error for Figure 7 as specified in Appendix F.3.1.

E6.justification: The corresponding performance curves, ablation results, encoder accuracies, and world-model transition probabilities are unchanged. Main and appendix figures retain the same findings; their relocation introduces no new or revised results.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1.3 adds a formal description of factored states and their Dynamic Bayesian Network transition factorization (v3 Equation 6), explaining its relationship to Ab-MDP. Existing Ab-MDP definitions, assumptions, and counterexamples remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions and claims about sample efficiency, transfer, interpretable world models, and learning abstraction components. The expanded discussion does not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly explains that discrete attributes cannot precisely capture continuous quantities such as position and velocity, while low-level policies can still use continuous features and actions. The existing limitation concerning supervised object mappings is retained.

D1.justification: Implementation details, architecture, data processing, hardware disclosures, hyperparameters, and resource links are unchanged (Appendices A, C, D, and G; Tables 7–10). Repositioned technical material supplies no additional reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B.1.3 add factored-MDP positioning and four references: Boutilier et al. (1995, 1999), Guestrin et al. (2003), and Degris and Sigaud (2013). The addition distinguishes action-dependent transition factorizations from Ab-MDP's item-change actions and learned dynamics.

P1.justification: Localized expansions affect related work, Appendix B.1.3, and the discussion, with an added closing paragraph. Affiliations, acknowledgments, and the publication header are updated. The section hierarchy and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Existing figures and tables are repositioned as text reflows, while their designs, axes, legends, and captions remain unchanged. For example, Table 7 now appears alongside Section G.1, and Table 10 moves after Figures 35–36.

improvement.justification: v3 improves research positioning through the explicit factored-MDP comparison in Section 5 and Appendix B.1.3, and clarifies applicability boundaries through the discrete-attribute limitation in Section 6. These are useful, limited improvements to context and scope; the method, experiments, and supporting results remain unchanged.
